articles.title: Jaylen Brown Injury Update, Latest on 76ers Star's Status for NBA Cup Game vs. Pacers
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown will miss Friday's NBA Cup game against the Indiana Pacers after leaving Wednesday's game with a hamstring injury, per ESPN's Kris Rhim.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown will miss Friday's NBA Cup game against the Indiana Pacers after leaving Wednesday's game with a hamstring injury, per ESPN's Kris Rhim .

Meanwhile, Joel Embiid is questionable as he continues to deal with an illness.

The 76ers ruled Brown out for the remainder of Wednesday's contest against the Miami Heat with hamstring tightness after he played 17 minutes against the Eastern Conference foe. As the ESPN broadcast captured, he appeared to be in pain following a jump shot:

Brown struggled prior to the setback and was an ugly 2-of-8 from the field and 0-of-1 from deep for six points, one rebound and one assist.

It was a far cry from his recent play, as he dropped 31 points in back-to-back contests against the Pacers and Brooklyn Nets before scoring 20 points in a loss to the Portland Trail Blazers. On the season, Brown is averaging 22.4 points, 6.3 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.3 steals per game on the campaign.

With Embiid (when healthy), LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe, the 76ers don't necessarily need Brown to dominate on a nightly basis like the Boston Celtics did last season when Jayson Tatum was sidelined.

Still, Philadelphia's ceiling is much higher when Brown is on the floor.

He is one of the best two-way players in the league with the ability to hit from the outside, drive the lane, take advantage of openings when defenders collapse on the other stars and guard the opponent's best players on the defensive side.

Fortunately for the 76ers, it is still early in the season in mid-November. There is no need to rush Brown back and risk further injury, and they will surely take a cautious approach following this setback.

For now, look for Maxey and James to carry more of the offense while Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope see more playing time.

articles.title: Líderes cristianos atacan a la "MAGA Barbie" de la WNBA por unas fotos: "Se sexualiza casi al nivel de..."
articles.standfirst: Sophie Cunningham concedió un reportaje a Maxim en el que, a pesar de hablar sobre su fe en Cristo, ha molestado a líderes cristianos que han criticado sus fotos "al nivel de la pornografía"
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham concedió un reportaje a Maxim en el que, a pesar de hablar sobre su fe en Cristo, ha molestado a líderes cristianos que han criticado sus fotos "al nivel de la pornografía"
articles.body: La mediática Sophie Cunningham, que se ha convertido en agente libre tras ser la escudera de Caitlin Clark en las Indiana Fever de la WNBA, ha provocado el descontento de un grupo de líderes cristianos tras participar en una sesión de fotos para la revista 'Maxim' en la que posó en topless. La conocida como la "MAGA (Make America Great Again) Barbie" de la WNBA, por su apoyo público a Donald Trump y sus polémica declaraciones en contra de la participación de mujeres trans en categorías femeninas, habló abiertamente en la entrevista sobre lo que busca en un esposo y subrayó la importancia de encontrar a alguien que comparta su fe: "Tengo estándares muy altos para mi futuro esposo. Debe ser alguien centrado en Cristo, capaz de guiarme en mi caminar con Jesús". "Busco a alguien amable, seguro de sí mismo y firme. Busco a un hombre que pueda impulsarme en mi fe, que sea leal y que, además, ame cada pequeño aspecto de mi persona", subrayó. Sophie Cunningham confesó que le encantaría convertirse algún día en la comisionada de la WNBA, argumentando que el puesto debería ser ocupado por una exjugadora que entienda tanto las necesidades de las deportistas como el lado comercial de la liga. Otros planes tras su retirada de las pistas pasan por explorar el mundo de los comentarios deportivos (algo que ya probó en 2026), los pódcasts y ser entrenadora. Sophie Cunningham expresó su interés en convertirse en la "próxima chica Bond". El exnadador Riley Gaines, conocido activista conservador, ha propuesto a la "MAGA Barbie" como candidata a "chica Bond". La última "chica Bond", un personaje llamado Doctora Madeleine Swann, fue interpretada por la actriz Léa Seydoux en la película de 2021 'Sin tiempo para morir' (No Time To Die). A pesar de estas declaraciones líderes conservadores cristianos expresaron su desacuerdo con el hecho de que Sophie Cunningham posara en topless para 'Maxim'. "Ya no puedo compartir la opinión de quienes instan a las mujeres jóvenes a considerarla un modelo a seguir. No querría que mi propia hija o mis nietas hicieran algo así. El hecho de que ella se sexualice, casi al nivel de la pornografía, en las fotografías para la revista 'Maxim' hace que eso sea imposible. Me desconcierta por qué alguien haría algo así", declaró Robert George, jurista conservador católico y profesor en la Universidad de Princeton, en el 'Christian Post'. El evangelista Justin Peters denunció que "existe una falta de discernimiento entre los líderes del mundo evangélico, que elogiamos y damos plataforma automáticamente a cualquier celebridad que sea capaz de pronunciar el nombre de Jesús, sin tomarnos el tiempo de ver si su profesión de fe da algún fruto. Siempre, siempre termina volviéndose en nuestra contra. Por más veces que veamos repetirse la misma historia, nunca aprendemos". Sophie Cunningham le explicó a Drew Hanlen, en su podcast 'No Hesitation', las reservas que tuvo en un primer momento para posar para 'Maxim'. "Bueno, fue muy curioso porque, en mi propio mundo —no sé—, simplemente no estaba familiarizada con 'Maxim'. Se pusieron en contacto conmigo y les pasé la propuesta a mis agentes. Al principio, su respuesta fue: '¡Ni hablar!'. Me preguntaron: '¿Qué estás haciendo?'. Y yo les dije: '¿A qué se refieren?'. Resulta que ellos no sabían que 'Maxim' había cambiado su enfoque. Pensaban en la antigua 'Maxim', que es —bueno, hay que decirlo— una revista para hombres. Yo les dije: '¡Dios mío, chicos! Jamás se me ocurriría hacer algo así'. Pero, una vez que supieron que habían cambiado su enfoque, realizamos la sesión de fotos en Indianápolis. Me lo pasé genial; fue una experiencia increíble. De hecho, esos pantalones de cuero que llevo puestos costaban, si no me equivoco, unos 27.000 dólares. ¡Y hicieron falta cuatro personas para ayudarme a ponérmelos!" recuerda. Sophie Cunningham celebró en su cuenta de Instagram su portada en 'Maxim' con una publicación en su cuenta de Instagram: "¿Jugar a disfrazarse a los 30 años y terminar siendo la protagonista de la portada de una revista?». ¡Vaya! ¡Esto no ha hecho más que empezar! ¡Gracias, Maxim por contar conmigo como chica de portada! Me he divertido". Sophie Cunningham le reveló a Theo Von algo alarmante: ha recibido amenazas y ha sido víctima de acoso. La escudera de Caitlin Clark en las Indiana Fever asegura que el FBI está vigilando a unas 20 personas en relación con su seguridad. Un hombre de 49 años fue detenido en junio y enfrenta cargos graves por acoso e intimidación, además de un cargo menor por hostigamiento.

articles.title: Dennis Rodman said Bulls players' wives asked to party with him almost every night
articles.summary: Rodman said Bulls players' wives wanted to party with him almost every night.
articles.body:
Bridging the gap between the players and their better halves? Sometimes that matters for team chemistry, too.

In Chicago, Dennis Rodman did, in a way. At least that's the role the Chicago Bulls players' wives handed him. They came to him almost every night. Always with the same question, too, before following the Worm's lead.

Rodman himself talked about it during a 2019 appearance on "The Breakfast Club."

The Worm took the studio back to his second of three seasons in Chicago, the 1996-07 season. By then he already had one ring with the Michael Jordan-led Bulls . Two more would follow. By Rodman's account, something "amazing" was going on at the time. It happened off the court.

"All the guys are married and stuff like that and all the wives will come to me and say, 'Dennis, where [are] you going out tonight?'" the two-time Defensive Player of the Year recalled .

Not only that. Once he'd likely let them in on his plans for the night, the wives tagged along quite often. That is, judging by what Dennis said next.

"They asked to go out with me almost every night," he remarked.

And since the Worm went out almost every night himself, it's safe to assume they joined him more often than not.

Say you happened to be out in Chicago at night back then. Judging by Rodman's account, this is roughly what it would have looked like. Depending on which part of the Bulls you crossed paths with, that was.

There was the Worm (sometimes in drag, by his own telling) with the players' wives. At a club. Or at a gay bar, if you ask the Hall of Famer.

The players, meanwhile, bar their starting forward, would head over to restaurants. All corporate, Rodman said. Wearing "suits and stuff like that."

Talk about a tale of two worlds. And you can probably guess which one the team's superstar belonged to. Jordan once made it clear that he wasn't "the partying type."

Rodman found it amazing. But did the other Bulls share his opinion?

Hard to know. Another story he shared offers a pretty good idea, though.

In 2018, Dennis sat down with "The Athletic." He went back over those nights. The wives. The bars. And how late it all went.

As for their husbands? Rodman's memory had them pretty relaxed about the whole thing. They, after all, knew where their better halves were.

Out with Dennis Rodman, of all people. Sometimes, though, a teammate came along, too. Back in San Antonio, Jack Haley sat next to Rodman. Didn't get a word out of him. For three weeks, actually.

Then one night the Worm invited Haley and his wife out for a drink . Their destination? A gay bar with male dancers. Haley even slipped one of them a dollar in his G-string, so it seems they've bonded pretty quickly.

articles.title: Warriors' Yaxel Admits He Was 'Upset' by NBA Rookie Rankings and Praises Kings' Darius Acuff Jr.
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star Yaxel Lendeborg took it a little personally when he read his position in NBA.com's newest Rookie Ladder.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star Yaxel Lendeborg took it a little personally when he read his position in NBA.com's newest Rookie Ladder .

"I saw the rankings today. I was No. 4," he told The Athletic's Devon Henderson . "I was a little upset about that."

Lendeborg did have plenty of praise for Sacramento Kings guard Darius Acuff Jr., who's sitting atop the Rookie Ladder.

"(Acuff) definitely got overlooked," Lendeborg said of the No. 7 overall pick. "Mine makes a lot more sense than his because I'm a little older, but he's the same age as all those guys and putting up the same kind of numbers. I don't know how you could pass up on him."

While the Kings are last in the Western Conference, it's not taking too much shine away from Acuff, who's averaging 24.4 points and playing nearly 37 minutes a night.

"I don't know how he's doing it so well," Lendeborg said. "For him, he's probably been dealing with that his whole life. Honestly, me, I've never really had that. I've always played off of somebody. It's different.

"I can only imagine how long it took him to adapt. It's crazy to see."

Like Acuff, Lendeborg is exceeding expectations out of the gate, but his performance is beginning to suffer a bit with Stephen Curry out of the lineup. He has shot 33.7 percent from the floor and averaged 13.7 points since Curry went down.

Acuff and Lendeborg crossed paths Wednesday night in NBA Cup play. Acuff nearly had a double-double, finishing with 22 points and nine assists. Lendeborg dropped a solid 15 points and eight rebounds.

Lendeborg at least claimed some bragging rights in the form of a 129-110 victory.

articles.title: No. 18 USC basketball drops its first game of the season in upset loss to unranked Utah State
articles.summary: The Trojans are now 7-1 and will take on Washington next Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Utah State Aggies are thankful to still be undefeated after their Thanksgiving matchup against No. 18 USC. The Aggies won 78-74 and moved to 7-0. The Trojans entered the game undefeated at 7-0 but suffered their first loss of the season.

This marked back-to-back close games for the Trojans. On Wednesday, USC narrowly beat unranked South Carolina 71-69, needing a late fourth-quarter comeback to secure the win.

That luck ran out Thursday night against Utah State in the Acrisure Series at Acrisure Arena in Palm Springs, California.

USC sophomore guard Alijah Arenas, son of former NBA guard Gilbert Arenas, led the Trojans in scoring yet again. He dropped 33 points and added 3 rebounds, 2 assists and a block.

The game was close on the stat sheet. USC shot 48% from the field and 32% from beyond the arc, compared to 45% and 29% for Utah State. The biggest difference between the teams was at the free-throw line. The Aggies made 18-of-22 attempts, while the Trojans took only 11 and made six.

Utah State was led by senior guard Mason Falslev, who finished with a team-high 27 points. Kingston Tosi provided a spark off the bench, adding 15 points and eight boards.

The Trojans will be back in action Wednesday against Washington (5-2, 0-0 Big Ten). Utah State will look to stay undefeated, taking on New Mexico (4-2, 0-0 Mountain West) on Sunday.

articles.title: No. 6 UCLA loses by 15 to unranked Saint Mary's for first loss of the season
articles.summary: Saint Mary's picked up a statement win that could easily factor into NCAA tournament seeding come March.
articles.body:
It is a bad day to be a ranked college basketball team based in Los Angeles.

Shortly after No. 18 USC was upset by unranked Utah State , the No. 6 UCLA Bruins lost to unranked Saint Mary's, 85-70.

The Bruins entered the matchup 6-0, but the Gaels had the right game plan, leading by 10 at halftime, and sustained that effort throughout the second half. UCLA kept it close at first, but Saint Mary's turned it on in the end.

Jaylen Petty led UCLA with 15 points, 7 boards and 1 assist. Xavier Booker added 14 points and eight boards.

The Bruins' problem was shooting from beyond the arc. UCLA shot 43% overall but just 29% from deep, hitting 5-of-16 attempts. By comparison, Saint Mary's shot 57% overall and 54% from 3-point range, knocking down 15-of-28 attempts.

Jeremy Dent-Smith led the Gaels with 21 points. One of the bigger sparks in the game came from Darius Bivins, who provided 16 points and five assists off the bench.

UCLA will look to shake off this loss as the Bruins return to action Tuesday, hosting Oregon for their first conference game of the season. Then, UCLA has a big non-conference matchup against No. 22 Gonzaga the following Saturday.

The win moved Saint Mary's to 7-1, as the Gaels have won five straight. They will next take on Hofstra on Tuesday. This victory over UCLA feels like one of those that we will remember at the end of the season when we break down Saint Mary's NCAA tournament résumé.

articles.title: Unforgiving rim denies Arkansas a miracle comeback against Michigan State on Thanksgiving
articles.summary: No. 11 Michigan State escaped with a 70-67 Thanksgiving win after Jordan Smith Jr.’s potential tying three rattled out in the final seconds.
articles.body: With 1:18 left in a game played on Thanksgiving, Arkansas trailed No. 11 Michigan State by 10 and the Spartans were at the free-throw line. If you’d offered John Calipari one shot to send the game to overtime, I’m guessing he’d have taken it before you finished the question. Well, he got his shot. Jordan Smith Jr. pulled up from 29 feet, and the ball found just about every part of the rim at Little Caesars Arena before it finally bounced out. Michigan State escaped Detroit with a 70-67 win to move to 6-1, and Arkansas fell to 4-3. Arkansas took a 31-27 lead into halftime, pushed it to eight early in the second half and still led 47-40 with 13:31 left. If you’re a Michigan State fan who watched the Spartans lose at Tennessee nine days earlier, I can’t blame you for thinking, "Uh-oh." They’d made all of three baskets in the second half in Knoxville and shot 18% for the game. MICHIGAN STATE'S PUTRID SHOOTING PERFORMANCE IN LOSS TO TENNESSEE PRODUCES LAUGHABLE FINAL BOX SCORE Down seven in Detroit, Jeremy Fears Jr. hit a three. Then he found Jesse McCulloch for a hook shot and Coen Carr for the dunk that tied it. Michigan State scored 15 straight, and by the time Kur Teng buried his third three in less than two minutes, the Spartans led 64-51 with 4:55 left. That’s a 24-4 run. The same team that went 3-for-26 after halftime at Tennessee went 17-for-21 (81%) in the second half against Arkansas. Michigan State still led 68-58 when Fears stepped to the line with 1:18 left. He missed the front end of a one-and-one, but Arkansas still needed 10 points just to pull even. COLLEGE BASKETBALL GETS A NEW NO. 1 AS THREE TEAMS FALL OUT OF THE AP TOP FIVE IN A SINGLE WEEK So how did the Razorbacks make it interesting in the final seconds? For starters, Michigan State just couldn’t grab a defensive rebound. The Razorbacks missed two threes on the same possession before Billy Richmond III tipped the ball in with 1:03 to go. Then Smith picked off a Fears pass. On the ensuing possession, Arkansas rebounded a missed free throw AND a missed three before Smith found Richmond for the three that cut it to 68-64. Arkansas gets a very generous and-one Jeremy Fears Jr. made both free throws with 16 seconds left to put Michigan State back up six. Then came the call I’d still be asking about if I were Tom Izzo. Smith drove to the basket and spun past Fears for a layup. The officials called Fears for a foul, counted the basket and gave Smith a chance to cut it to three with 10 seconds left. Did Fears foul Smith? Absolutely. Smith still had his back to the basket and was about 13 feet from the hoop when the contact came. Smith finished his spin, took another full step and then laid the ball in. How much continuation are we giving this guy? Even the CBS crew thought the foul should have been ruled on the floor. Smith made the free throw with 10 seconds left, Fears missed the front end of a one-and-one with eight seconds left, and guess who came down with the rebound? Smith had six seconds and the length of the floor to find a three. From 29 feet, he came about as close as you can get. A Thanksgiving bad beat for Michigan State bettors If you laid 5.5 with Michigan State, how good did you feel with 1:18 left? Your team was up 10, and you had a career 81% free-throw shooter at the line. You could give up a couple of garbage-time buckets and still cash. Fears missed the front end, Arkansas grabbed four offensive rebounds in two possessions, and Michigan State threw the ball away in between. And after all that? You were still covering when Fears hit both free throws to make it 70-64 with 16 seconds left. It took that generous continuation call to put Arkansas back inside the number. Then your 81% free-throw shooter went back to the line with eight seconds left and missed the front end of another one-and-one. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD That left Michigan State bettors rooting for the same guy who’d just cost them the cover. If Smith’s three drops, you get five more minutes to win by six. If you had Arkansas +5.5, on the other hand, you had every reason to cheer when that ball finally bounced out. Which probably raised a fair question from across the Thanksgiving table: "Wait, didn’t you bet on Arkansas?"

articles.title: El Movistar Estudiantes juega con ADN NBA para levantar el vuelo
articles.standfirst: La estadounidense Kendall Cooper, prima de Tony Smith y de Malik Monk, espera un Magariños lleno ante el Ibaeta en un encuentro crucial
articles.summary: La estadounidense Kendall Cooper, prima de Tony Smith y de Malik Monk, espera un Magariños lleno ante el Ibaeta en un encuentro crucial
articles.body: El Movistar Estudiantes comenzó la temporada en Liga Femenina Endesa disparando las expectativas con dos victorias en las dos primeras jornadas. Sin embargo, desde entonces las chicas de Isaac Fernández no han conseguido volver al camino del triunfo. Las Women in Black han mejorado en juego y prestaciones y ahora lo quieren trasladar al marcador final con una victoria ante el Ibaeta. Para ello quieren un Movistar Academy Magariños lleno este sábado. Una grada que empuje a un equipo en el que está destacando Kendall Cooper y que quiere remontar el vuelo al ritmo que marca la jugadora estadounidense. Máxima anotadora y segunda mejor reboteadora del conjunto estudiantil, la pívot de Carson está exhibiendo cualidades para el baloncesto que le vienen casi desde la cuna. De hecho le vienen por la parte de su familia materna. Una rama de su familia con ADN NBA como el que lucen Tony Smith, exjugador de Lakers con los que llegó a disputar la final de la NBA, y Malik Monk, número 11 del draft y que sigue en activo en las filas de los Sacramento Kings. Dos jugones que son el espejo familiar de Cooper. "Son mis primos por parte de madre. Somos muchos en ese lado de la familia”, apunta Cooper. "Su consejo es que nunca cambie mi forma de jugar. Siempre me dicen que esté concentrada y que juegue a mi manera. En el baloncesto profesional siempre hay gente que intente cambiar tu estilo de juego para que encajes en sus moldes. Lo que me dicen es que no cambie". Su primo Tony no sólo tuvo experiencia en la NBA durante su carrera deportiva. Tras pasar por Lakers, Heat, Suns y Hornets, Smith recaló en el TAU Vitoria en 1997. Apenas estuvo ocho partidos en la escuadra baskonista (9,5 puntos y 3,1 asistencias en 28 minutos) pero se le quedó grabado el ritmo de juego en el baloncesto español. “Una de las pocas cosas que Tony me dijo cuando le dije que venía a jugar a España es que estuviera preparada para correr, que aquí se juega muy rápido. Y no mentía al respecto. Creo que le subestimé cuando lo decía”, asegura entre risas la exjugadora de los Blue Devils de Duke. Adaptada ya a la velocidad de juego Cooper no se deja nada en el depósito cada vez que salta a la cancha. Por eso es una de las preferidas de la grada de un Magariños que espera ver lleno este sábado. “Cada vez que estoy en la cancha, lo que ves es quien soy. Me gusta competir, así que me esfuerzo al máximo para darle el 100 % de mí al equipo. Y si siento que todavía me queda algo de energía, lo doy todo”. Ahora sólo queda que ese esfuerzo se traduzca en una nueva victoria que daría vuelo a las colegiales. Para ello no existe una receta mágica, aunque Cooper da las claves para dar un paso adelante: “No existe una receta fija para que los equipos mejoren, pero, en nuestro caso, creo que necesitamos anotar. Trabajamos bien en conjunto en otros aspectos del juego; simplemente necesitamos meter el balón en el aro”.

articles.body: Las cábalas son múltiples a falta de tres partidos de clasificación y con tantas selecciones implicadas, pero España sabe que ganando este domingo (18.00 h, TDP y Vamos) en el Fontes do Sar a Grecia, si además supera el basket-average del partido de Atenas (-3), el pase al Mundial de Qatar 2027 estaría prácticamente en el bolsillo. Con esa sensación volará en las próximas horas desde Podgorica a Santiago, donde se reunirá con los internacionales del Madrid, Pradilla y Abalde, y con el del Anadolu Efes, Santi Yusta. Los tres jugaron sus partidos de Euroliga el miércoles. A España le saldrían las matemáticas si además de ganar le sonríen otros resultados: Georgia supera a Portugal en Tiblisi y Montenegro gane a Ucrania en Riga. En esas coordenadas, la clasificación puede estar prácticamente asegurada. El 'visado' a Qatar podría estar en la frontera de las siete victorias, con eso debe bastar. Una más lo asegura matemáticamente. A España le quedan, además del partido en Santiago ante el apurado combinado heleno, viajar a Portugal (26 de febrero, en Matosinhos) y recibir a Montenegro (1 de marzo, en una sede aún por decidir). Es jornada electoral, pero el Fontes do Sar estará lleno (quedaban dos decenas de localidades) para el encuentro que no sólo puede casi garantizar la presencia de España en el décimo Mundial de su historia, todos desde 1973 en Filipinas. La selección de Mateo puede apuntillar a la griega, que se presenta en Galicia apesadumbrada tras su derrota ante Georgia del jueves (88-92) con un pésimo juego. Spanoulis, el seleccionador heleno, no daba crédito para explicar la dinámica derrotista que envuelve a su equipo y que le afecta sobre la cancha, como ocurrió ante los georgianos. “Creo que tenemos que ver el partido contra Georgia y contar cuántas bandejas fallamos. Más de 10 o 12. Así es el baloncesto. Tenemos que seguir adelante. Es una derrota dura, y punto. Todo lo que podía salir mal, salió mal. Cometimos una violación de ocho segundos. Permitimos un triple de un jugador alto que nunca antes había anotado uno...” Si España lo tiene en la mano y podría meterse este domingo con un poco de fortuna, Grecia necesita la proeza de ganar al menos dos de los tres partidos que le quedan. Son urgencias épicas para una selección acostumbrada a estar en las grandes competiciones. No falla en un Mundial desde Indianápolis 2002. La ausencia es devastadora: tampoco podrá competir en Los Ángeles 2028. España está avisada de su peligrosidad, ahora que vive a la desesperada. “Sabemos que el partido del domingo es muy importante. Nos jugamos mucho los dos equipos. Podemos dar un paso definitivo hacia el Mundial”, resumía Pierre Oriola.

articles.title: Oregon men's basketball offense stalls late in loss to Texas Tech
articles.summary: Oregon failed to make a field goal in the final five minutes as Texas Tech rallied to beat the Ducks 62-59 in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
Oregon's offense went cold and was unable to hold a late lead as No. 5 Texas Tech rallied to win Nov. 26 during a Players Era 16 Tournament men's basketball game at Michelob ULTRA Arena in Las Vegas.

The Ducks didn't make a field goal in the final five minutes as the Red Raiders overcame a five-point deficit to win 62-59, sending Oregon to its third straight loss.

Jasper Johnson tied his season high with 18 points to lead the Ducks (3-3), and Andrew Meadow scored 13.

See photos from Oregon men's basketball vs Oregon State at Moda Center

Oregon trailed by 13 in the second half but went on 19-2 run to take a 54-49 advantage with 7:24 to play.

A layup by Fred Payne with 5:19 left in the game put the Ducks ahead 56-51, but that was their last field goal of the game as they missed their final five attempts, including a 3-point miss by Johnson with three seconds to play that would've tied the score.

Oregon outshot Texas Tech 42%-38.9% but was outrebounded 34-32 and allowed the Red Raiders to get 14 offensive rebounds and score 17 second-chance points.

The Ducks did have a season-high seven blocks, with Taylor Bol Bowen and Pharaoh Compton getting three each.

Oregon trailed by double digits at halftime. The score was 25-24 Texas Tech with just under four minutes to play in the first half, but the Ducks were outscored 13-3 over the final 3:24 and trailed 38-27 at the break.

What's next for the Oregon men's basketball team

The Ducks have one more game in Las Vegas at 12:30 p.m. Friday when they get an early season look at Big Ten opponent Maryland. The Terrapins are 3-4 after a 75-71 loss to San Diego State Thursday.

Chris Hansen covers University of Oregon football, men's basketball, track and field, cross country and softball for The Register-Guard. You can reach him at chansen@registerguard.com.

articles.title: Nets’ Moritz Wagner to miss Raptors game with knee issue
articles.summary: The Nets frontcourt is going from thin to downright worrisome, with backup center Moritz Wagner out with a left knee issue.
articles.body:
TORONTO — The Nets frontcourt is going from thin to downright worrisome, with backup center Moritz Wagner out with a knee issue.

Wagner left Wednesday's win in Milwaukee in the first quarter and was ruled out with left knee soreness. Now the only pure center the Nets have besides Day'Ron Sharpe will miss Friday's game in Toronto with left knee injury management.

"I was about to sub him in, and I saw him limping, and I was like I got to save him from himself," coach Jordi Fernández said. "He was there to do whatever it took for his team and his teammates, and at the end I decided to not bring him back in.

"The good thing — the great thing — is he was cheering for everybody. He was cheering for Grant [Nelson] the whole time, and that means a lot for the group, and it speaks to the type of person he is."

It's the same knee in which Wagner suffered a torn left ACL on Dec. 21, 2024. That ended his season and sidelined him until January 2026.

Sharpe logged 31-plus minutes Wednesday and could be asked to shoulder another heavy load against the Raptors, who've lost seven of eight.

He had 11 points and a season-high 14 rebounds against the Bucks, his fifth double-double to match his total from all of last season. Sharpe also added five assists and four steals.

"My effort, my motor is always going to be me," said Sharpe. "This is part of my game. It's a part of who I am, the hard work I play with, the hard effort I play with."

Nelson had just one point against the Bucks, but six rebounds, including three on the offensive glass. He was a plus-6 in just 13:04.

"The offensive rebounds for us were huge, six rebounds. He was a plus on the court, a great 13 minutes. He definitely was a big part of this win," said Fernández.

"Grant obviously not necessarily was expecting to go there for as much as he did," added Egor Dëmin. "But with Moe being out of the game, he had to go out there and compete. I talked to him in halftime and he was extremely ready to go, and just do what's best for the team."

Noah Clowney broke out of his extended funk against Milwaukee.

The young forward had 17 points and finished plus-14, both season highs. He shot 7-for-13, grabbed five rebounds and scored nine points in the fourth quarter.

"It was great to see him be aggressive, seeing the matchup he has and being aggressive off the closeout and just letting the ball fly when he had opportunity," said Sharpe. "He helps us out a lot, especially with the defensive presence he brings, his versatility on the offensive end. We just need him to continue to be confident in who he is and bring it out every night."

articles.title: Louisville HC Pat Kelsey gushes about ‘special’ Cardinals team after dramatic St. John’s win
articles.summary: The Louisville Cardinals survived a wild finish against the St. John’s Red Storm on Thanksgiving night, and head coach Pat Kelsey couldn’t stop raving about...
articles.body:
The Louisville Cardinals survived a wild finish against the St. John's Red Storm on Thanksgiving night , and head coach Pat Kelsey couldn't stop raving about his squad afterward.

No. 25 Louisville knocked off No. 13 St. John's 93-90 in the semifinals of the Players Era 16 Tournament at Michelob ULTRA Arena in Las Vegas, with Adrian Wooley burying a fallaway corner 3-pointer at the buzzer to hand the Red Storm their first loss of the season .

After the game , Kelsey explained what makes this group so special.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"This team is special… They're a group of dudes that just care about each other and just go to work like pros every single day. We don't have parent problems, we don't have agent problems… This team is a joy to coach. And they're fun to be around. It's player-led, just two unbelievably dynamic personalities and young men and leaders that are up here right now," Kelsey said, via The Field of 68.

The Cardinals had to dig deep to pull this one out. Louisville raced out to a 57-39 halftime lead and went up by as many as 24 points, but St. John's stormed back in the second half. Ian Jackson eventually tied the game with two free throws with 13 seconds left, setting the stage for Wooley's heroics.

Seth Trimble was the driving force for Louisville , pouring in a game-high 33 points on 12-of-19 shooting off the bench. Wooley finished with 19 points on 4-of-8 shooting from deep, while Karter Knox added 15 points and Flory Bidunga chipped in 12 points and nine rebounds.

For St. John's, Jackson scored 18 points, and Keyshawn Hall posted a double-double with 17 points and 10 rebounds.

The victory improved Louisville to 5-1 on the season. Still, Kelsey made it clear there is no time to dwell on it.

"And that was a big win, right? It was a big win for a lot of reasons. But we're in tournament play, and we celebrate it in the locker room. We turn the page, and we gotta get ready for our next opponent. And we're gonna play three games in three days," Kelsey added.

Louisville will face Tennessee in the championship game on Friday.

articles.title: Nate Oats reveals 1 thing Alabama needs to fix after beating Kansas State
articles.summary: Alabama improved to 6-1 after beating Kansas State, 104-91, in the Players Era 16 Tournament at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Thursday. The No. 15 Crimson T...
articles.body:
Alabama improved to 6-1 after beating Kansas State, 104-91, in the Players Era 16 Tournament at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Thursday.

The No. 15 Crimson Tide improved to 6-1, bouncing back from the loss to Baylor on Tuesday.

Seven players scored in double digits for Alabama, led by Qayden Samuel's 14 points off the bench. He added six rebounds. Amari Allen had 12 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, and two steals, while Drew Fielder and Anderson Diaz also scored a dozen apiece.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Coach Nate Oats was happy with his players' response coming off a defeat, as reported by BamaOnLine's Blake Byler.

"Good to get a win. We needed that after the loss to Baylor. Defensively, we're making strides. I thought we did a decent job outside of a few things," said Oats.

He, however, also pointed out a room for improvement , as quoted by BamaCentral's Hunter De Siver.

"We handled the physicality a lot better today than Tuesday. But at the end of the day, we've got to guard without fouling," added Oats.

Alabama committed 28 fouls. Kansas State went 28-of-37 from the free-throw line.

The Wildcats committed two more fouls than the Crimson Tide, who went 37-of-45 from the charity stripe.

Kansas State cut Alabama's lead to 10 points with 5:41 remaining in the second half. Allen, however, sank four straight free throws to fend off the rally.

The Crimson Tide led by as much as 19 points. They shot 51% from the field. They survived despite having 21 turnovers, which the Wildcats converted to 20 points.

Alabama will face Miami for fifth place on Friday.

articles.summary: The Detroit Pistons will have to go another NBA Cup matchup without starting point guard Cade Cunningham. Detroit has ruled out Cunningham for Friday’s game...
articles.body:
The Detroit Pistons will have to go another NBA Cup matchup without starting point guard Cade Cunningham . Detroit has ruled out Cunningham for Friday's game at Little Caesars Arena against the Milwaukee Bucks due to his ongoing knee injury . This will be the third game Cunningham is forced to miss because of the ailment.

Cunningham went through shootaround before Tuesday's game against the Orlando Magic. He was listed on the injury report as probable prior to tipoff. After warming up with the team, the Pistons decided to sit the All-Star point guard for rest and recovery. Detroit head coach J.B. Bickerstaff briefly spoke on Cunningham's status before the contest against Orlando.

"He's battling through a lot, and I'll leave it at that. He's gonna go out and compete and give us what he's got, but he's fighting through a lot," Bickerstaff explained.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Detroit continues to battle through the regular season as injuries have plagued some of their most important players. All-Star center Jalen Duren has been out since October due to a hamstring injury. Shooting guard Duncan Robinson has been out for the last five games after suffering a quad injury.

The Pistons are 11-6 and have found roster adjustments to keep winning despite injuries. Bickerstaff has used seven different starting lineups and has given every player on the roster playing time to fill in. Relying on the next man up mentality has been a big calling card for the Pistons this season.

There is currently no timeline for Cunningham's return to the court. The Pistons normally are patient and do not rush back injured players.

articles.title: Luka Dončić is a scoring machine. The NBA has rarely seen anything like it.
articles.summary: Most NBA teams wouldn’t choose to let a player considered perhaps the greatest ever walk away in free agency.
articles.body: Most NBA teams wouldn’t choose to let a player considered perhaps the greatest ever walk away in free agency. Yet that’s exactly what the Lakers did last summer — because most NBA teams will never have a franchise pivot ready to go quite like Los Angeles did. Ever since Dallas stunningly traded Luka Dončić to the Lakers midway through the 2025 season and the Lakers paired the Slovenian superstar in his mid-20s with LeBron James, the all-time great who is a generation older, the NBA waited to see when the Lakers would decide to put the team’s future on Dončić’s timeline. That moment officially arrived last summer, when the 41-year-old James left in free agency and the Lakers didn’t try to stop the move. There was no longer any doubt about which star the Lakers orbited. The only question was how comfortably Dončić would shoulder the championship expectations. Nearly a fifth of the way through the regular season, the results have been extraordinary enough to push Dončić into a pantheon of scorers alongside such hallowed names as Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan — and thrust the Lakers into the discussion as a serious challenger to the Western Conference’s pre-ordained championship contenders, the San Antonio Spurs and the Oklahoma City Thunder. Only Chamberlain (in 1961 and 1962), Rick Barry (1966), Jordan (1986), James Harden (2019) and Elgin Baylor (1960) have scored more points through their first 16 games of a season than Dončić’s 586 thus far. While facing Dončić during the last six years of his 14-year career, longtime NBA guard Reggie Jackson grew accustomed to his opponent’s tendencies and style, including feeling out a defense during the opening minutes. This season, “it’s kind of like he already knows all the answers,” Jackson told NBC News. “He comes out in the first quarter and he just he has his foot on the gas, and then from there, whether depending on what type of shot is going in, he kind of seems to play it off that.” Dončić is scoring more than a point per minute and a league-high 36.6 points per game by taking and making more 3-pointers (4.8 on 13.2 attempts per game) and free throws (8.8 on 10.2 per game) than anyone. His accuracy both beyond the 3-point line and inside it exceed his career averages. Dončić has called it enjoyable to score as much, but has said he’s more driven by winning. Iztok Franko, a data-driven Slovenian basketball analyst and author, has watched every game Dončić has played since he was a teenage sensation at Spain’s Real Madrid, and has seen Dončić produce a burst of high-scoring games before. Yet the combination of a hamstring injury that sidelined Dončić for both rounds of the Lakers’ postseason last spring and the team’s offseason decision to mold itself in his image had left Dončić “very motivated and hungry for this season,” Franko believes. “Especially because this is now his team, with all the makeover the Lakers did over the summer. Luka had the longest period without basketball in his career, and the man truly loves playing basketball, so I think he had a huge itch to play, to entertain us again,” Franko said. “He also missed the Slovenian National Team play in the summer for the first time since 2017 and fully focused on rehab and preparing for this season.” “So, I think all of that, plus the motivation for a good start, which was very important to avoid the noise, the criticism of the new team that would come if they would struggle out of the gate, contributed to him starting the way he did.” Rob Pelinka, the Lakers’ president of basketball operations, compared Dončić to an illusionist, he told the team’s broadcaster this month, because “every night he does something unexpected.” “If you look at the math or analytics of what he’s doing, it’s like in the same breath as Wilt Chamberlain. Like, did I just say that?” Pelinka said. “Like a modern-era player putting up those kind of numbers?” After Dončić had scored 42 points to beat Miami eight games into the season, Heat star and two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo called Dončić “one of the best scorers to play this game, if not the best.” Did he meant currently playing, or ever? “Of all time,” Antetokounmpo told reporters. “I feel like some people are scared to say that, but he’s got to be up there.” That game was one of Doncic’s seven already with 40 points or more. No other player has scored 40-plus more than four times this season. Any player scoring at a pace like that would face scrutiny over its sustainability, but with Dončić, such concerns are rooted in the reason why he is a Laker at all. When Dallas traded him in 2025 — after puzzlingly negotiating solely with the Lakers, without seeing what 28 other teams would offer — the Mavericks justified the decision partly by questioning Dončić’s commitment to conditioning. Dončić responded last season with a much publicized and revamped offseason workout regimen, but on nights when his jumper was not falling, he could also depend on James, the NBA’s all-time leading scorer, and up-and-coming sidekick Austin Reaves to step up in his place. Reaves is still a Laker, but with James gone the Lakers’ formula for success now hinges on Dončić to a degree rarely seen in NBA history. The NBA record for usage rate — a possession that ends in either a field goal attempt, a free throw attempt or a turnover by a certain player — is 41.6%, set by Russell Westbrook in 2017. Dončić is currently at 40.44%, by one measure, which if sustained would rank third all time. Dončić touches the ball nearly 84 times per game, nearly 14 more than Reaves, the next closest teammate, according to league tracking data. The strategy has paid off; of the 43 high-usage players who touch the ball more than 60 times per game, Dončić’s points-per-touch average ranks third best. “We live on a spaceship, and we’re going at the speed of light at all times when he’s on the court,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said. A team hasn’t empowered Dončić to this degree since he led Dallas to the 2024 NBA Finals, said an NBA scout not authorized to speak publicly about player evaluations. “I think the Lakers bought into the heliocentric style of play that the Mavericks tried to avoid at times” over concerns about his stamina, the scout said. “Credit to Luka for being in good enough shape to play that way the entire game.” But, the scout added, “the test will be if he can withstand this level of play for 65-plus games.” The Lakers have acknowledged the heavy burden. After Dončić scored 29 points on 28 field goal attempts during a loss to lowly Utah in November, Redick said that “the shot creation that is required from him takes its toll.” Perhaps as a result, his habits as a scorer have changed. Compared with his previous eight NBA seasons, Dončić is more reliant on 3-pointers, with 52% of his field goal attempts coming there and only 6% of his shots coming from within 3 feet of the rim, compared to his career rate of 15%. Franko believes the biggest difference that has sparked this scoring run and the Lakers’ 15-3 record is “him being healthy and continuing with his commitment to off court, diet, training plan that started in the summer of 2025,” he said. “That, along with the motivation to lead this team, to prove this new team is capable of being better than people expect it to be, I think resulted in the biggest on-court change, which is his commitment to defensive end, and to play faster.” “I think defensively he was very good for [a] majority of the games, and his buy-in there has been crucial for Lakers success so far,” Franko added. The Lakers’ commitment to Dončić as their leader was evident last summer, when teammates flew to Ljubljana, Slovenia, to spend several days training and hanging out with Dončić at his invitation. A Slovenian media outlet reported he had paid for his teammates’ chartered flight. The gesture was also symbolic: No other Laker is more responsible this season for whether the team can continue to fly high. “It just feels like almost anything he shoots, whether it’s a circus shot, or whether it’s a regular stepback 3, or it’s a tough look, it seems like everything he shoots is going to go in,” Lakers teammate Quentin Grimes said in early November, after Dončić had scored at least 37 points in five consecutive games. “It’s kind of surreal. I don’t think I’ve ever been on the court when everything somebody shoots, you think it’s going in.”

articles.title: New NBA Power Rankings, Plus Something Every Team Can Be Thankful For
articles.summary: The 2026-27 NBA season has made it through Thanksgiving. And though some teams are already essentially eliminated from playoff contention, every one has something to be thankful for.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season has made it through Thanksgiving. And though some teams are already essentially eliminated from playoff contention, every one has something to be thankful for.

Whether your favorite is near the top or bottom of the standings, we have some reasons for optimism today.

And of course, we've also sorted through and ordered all 30 organizations based on the criteria that have guided us for years: team and individual numbers, recent performance, championship chances, and plenty of subjectivity.

30. Milwaukee Bucks (2-17): Brayden Burries

A team with a dreadful record and an encouraging rookie, the Milwaukee Bucks picked up their second win of the season this week. And combo guard Brayden Burries had a heck of a line in it.

Against the Toronto Raptors and in under 30 minutes, Burries put up 14 points, 10 rebounds, four assists and three steals. He even had a block for good measure.

It's that kind of wide-ranging production that makes Burries so interesting. He's not your typical point guard. He's not a typical shooting guard. He's just a basketball player who consistently makes the right plays.

On the season, Burries is putting up 17.3 points, 8.8 rebounds (including 3.3 offensive rebounds), 4.0 assists and 1.3 steals per 75 possessions. Once he starts hitting threes consistently, he could get to star status awful quick.

29. Sacramento Kings (2-16): Darius Acuff

Darius Acuff shoots a lot. In fact, he probably shoots too much. This season, Luka Dončić and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander are the only players taking more field-goal attempts per game.

But there's something to be said for Acuff's ability to get to those shots. It's not like he's just crossing halfcourt and chucking the ball toward the rim. He's creating decent looks. On a lot of nights, he's hitting them.

From October 29 through November 18, he averaged 28.1 points and 7.9 assists, while shooting 39.0 percent from three. And in that stretch, he looked like a bona fide future superstar.

The more experience he gains, the more common those runs will become.

The Charlotte Hornets entered the season with expectations to be one of the best shooting teams in the NBA. And while they've certainly taken plenty (they're second in the league in attempts per game), they're not really falling yet. The Hornets are dead last in three-point percentage at 31.8.

But that number holding feels almost impossible.

At some point, Kon Knueppel will be back. And Brandon Miller, Naz Reid, Coby White and Royce O'Neale, who are all currently well below their career marks from three-point range, will start knocking down shots.

27. New Orleans Pelicans (5-14): The Core

Availability has been an issue for several of the New Orleans Pelicans' most important players for years. And that's crept into this season with Trey Murphy missing eight games already.

But New Orleans, despite once again having a terrible record and point differential, is still pretty good when it puts its best players on the floor together.

The sample size is small, but the Pelicans are plus-15.4 points per 100 possessions when Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy III and Herb Jones are all on the floor.

As you can see, the Brooklyn Nets are pretty routinely getting blown out, but the new anti-tanking rules have stripped that of having really any value.

Even more important, in Brooklyn's specific case, the Houston Rockets have swap rights over the Nets' first-rounder. Losing has no value for them.

That's made the minutes with Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle and Day'Ron Sharpe more important than they'd be in most other rebuilding contexts. Brooklyn fans should want to see some competitive basketball, and when those three are on the floor, the Nets are a respectable minus-1.3 points per 100 possessions.

Caleb Wilson looks like he has the potential to make some All-Star teams. He's already doing more on the ball than many expected at any point this year, but the Chicago Bulls probably gave him a little too much freedom before he went down with injury.

Wilson was playing an iso-heavy brand of ball, taking 16.2 shots in 30.8 minutes and only shooting 42.0 percent from the field. The Bulls were 1-9 in those games and routinely being blown away.

Since he left the rotation, Chicago is 5-3. The ball is moving more. It's finding veteran finishers more. Even the defense is a little more cohesive.

And though this certainly doesn't mean the Bulls should completely abandon their developmental approach with Wilson, it's a pretty good sign they shouldn't abandon team concepts when he plays either.

Taking some of the playmaking responsibilities off his plate, getting him some easier looks and still empowering him to occasionally color outside the lines should be the way forward after he returns from injury.

After the NBA levied its punishment for cap circumvention this past summer and stripped the Los Angeles Clippers of several future first-round picks, things felt pretty bleak for the organization.

But they were allowed to finalize the Kawhi Leonard trade, which restocked the asset cupboard a bit. And they have a couple of veterans playing well enough to bring them more picks before February's trade deadline.

The biggest surprise could be Brook Lopez, who's averaging 14.4 points and 5.1 rebounds in 24.0 minutes, while shooting 43.3 percent from three, in his age-38 season. Darius Garland (20.7 points and 6.4 assists) and Brandon Ingram (who recently made his season debut) could return some value too.

After showing signs of life ahead of last week's edition of the power rankings, the Utah Jazz went winless between then and now.

Especially since they're in the West, it's increasingly clear that this season, when Utah was finally supposed to turn a corner, is bound to end with another lottery pick (though this one could wind up being the Memphis Grizzlies).

But there are reasons for optimism, and they go by Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey. There's a noticeable pop in Utah's lineup featuring both. Their combined length and athleticism helps the Jazz defend at a respectable level .

And over his last 11 games, Peterson is starting to figure out the other end too. In that stretch, he's at 18.4 points, 4.8 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.1 steals in 30.3 minutes.

22. Indiana Pacers (6-12): Tyrese Haliburton

This one might seem a little weird, since Tyrese Haliburton has only appeared in four games, but the injury he's nursing now isn't a season-ender.

This current absence is just a reminder of how important he is to the team, and it has a light at the end of the tunnel (Haliburton himself hopes to be back before December).

This season, the Indiana Pacers are plus-4.0 points per 100 possessions when Haliburton is on the floor and minus-5.0 when he's off.

21. Toronto Raptors (6-11): The Eastern Conference

Kawhi Leonard has only appeared in two games. Alijah Martin and rookie Allen Graves are the only Toronto Raptors with 100-plus minutes and positive net rating swings ( seriously ). Despite a respectable season-long point differential, things are rough in Toronto.

But the Raptors are in the East, where a 6-11 start is far from damning. In fact, if the season ended today, they'd be in the play-in tournament.

So, if Toronto can simply get Leonard back and keep him on the floor for an extended stretch, it still has a real shot at a top-six finish.

The Orlando Magic may have lost their last game of the week against the Detroit Pistons, but they're 5-3 in their last eight.

And during this extended stretch without Paolo Banchero, it's become clear that Franz Wagner can and should take on even more playmaking responsibility.

In his last nine outings, Wagner is averaging 28.3 points, 7.8 assists and 7.6 rebounds.

Even Banchero's return should be seen as much as an opportunity to get Wagner another receiver as it is to shift the offense back into Banchero's hands.

It's mostly Anthony Davis who's making the Washington Wizards competitive this season, but it's the younger players who are offering some hope for the future.

Twenty-two-year-old Kyshawn George has been a steady-handed point forward all season, with averages of 17.8 points, 4.4 assists and 4.3 rebounds.

And in his last five games, the 2026 No. 1 pick, AJ Dybantsa, has put up 20.0 points, 9.2 rebounds and 4.8 assists.

Regardless of what happens for the rest of 2026-27, knowing that this is the forward combo of the future should generate some optimism in Wizards fans.

18. Cleveland Cavaliers (9-10): The Youth

For a team that entered 2026-27 fancying itself a title contender, you might think it's tough to find something to be thankful for in this sub-.500 start.

But Meleek Thomas, Tyrese Proctor and Jaylon Tyson actually made it pretty easy.

The first-, second- and third-year players are about the only sources of life for the Cleveland Cavaliers in a lot of games. All three are generally unselfish relative to their positions and roles. All three play hard. And in the event the Cavs decided to turn the page on this era, they'd have a pretty interesting young core to pivot to.

17. Golden State Warriors (10-8): Yaxel Lendeborg

His numbers have tailed off a bit since Stephen Curry left the rotation with an injury, but Yaxel Lendeborg starting his career as a borderline star has completely changed the outlook for Curry's twilight years.

The Golden State Warriors were seemingly drawing dead for 2026-27. The chances of them beating a team like the San Antonio Spurs in a playoff series still feel slim, but assuming everyone's healthy, there is indeed a chance.

And again, Lendeborg is a big part of that.

He's way ahead of schedule as a ball-in-hand creator. He's a good enough shooter to force defenses to respect him out there. His passing can be weaponized by Curry's shooting and off-ball movement.

If the Warriors have him, Curry, Jimmy Butler and one more helpful player from a Kristaps Porziņģis trade, they could be dangerous.

The Phoenix Suns are 8-3 in their last 11 games, and they have a second unit that plays a lot like last season's surprise team to thank for it.

Phoenix's point differential is worse ( a lot worse, actually) when Dillon Brooks, Devin Booker or Jalen Green is on the floor.

But last season's grit, shooting and unselfishness is abundant in reserves like Collin Gillespie, Jordan Goodwin, Luke Kennard and Ryan Dunn, all of whom have positive plus-minuses for the year.

15. Oklahoma City Thunder (10-9): The Next Few Weeks

Injuries have absolutely rocked the Oklahoma City Thunder, who are 2-7 in their last nine games, will likely be without Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace for the rest of this campaign and won't get Chet Holmgren back till around the new year.

But even with this version of the team, there's a pretty good chance OKC can string some wins together prior to Holmgren's return.

Each of the Thunder's next six games are against sub-.500 teams. Five are against the Milwaukee Bucks, Brooklyn Nets (twice), Sacramento Kings and Charlotte Hornets, some of the worst teams in the league.

If OKC can generate just a little momentum heading into a tougher stretch around Christmas and get Holmgren back a little after that, it could claw its way back to the title contenders' tier.

The Denver Nuggets may be the most enigmatic team in the NBA.

On one hand, in the last week and change, they beat the Boston Celtics and Houston Rockets in back-to-back games. They followed that with an overtime win over the Chicago Bulls, scoring 151 points. But that little three-game streak was bookended by two dreadful performances at home against the Phoenix Suns and Dallas Mavericks.

By halftime of Tuesday's loss, Denver fans were once again booing the lack of effort on display.

But instead of getting defensive, the Nuggets' best player this season took ownership of his team's uninspiring play.

Denver fans should take heart in this answer from Murray. There's been a vacuum of leadership since Michael Malone was fired, but this sounds like a player who might be able to fill it. And that's supported by what he's doing on the floor too.

Even after an off shooting night against Dallas, Murray is averaging 25.8 points, 5.7 assists and 3.3 threes, while shooting 45.6 percent from deep.

13. Dallas Mavericks (11-7): The Basketball Gods

Dallas Mavericks fans had about as much righteous indignation as you'll ever see from a fanbase in the wake of the to-this-day inexplicable Luka Dončić trade.

But they did not have to wait long for the Basketball Gods to put their organization back on the right track.

Just a few months after Nico Harrison torpedoed a title contender, Dallas won the lottery in Cooper Flagg's draft year. Just a few weeks into his second season, it's already clear the Mavs have another perennial MVP candidate. And this one has the potential to be a game-changing defender too.

After blowing out the Denver Nuggets (in Denver and in the NBA Cup), Flagg is up to 24.3 points, 6.7 assists, 6.3 rebounds and 1.8 steals per game this season.

Once he figures out how to consistently knock down threes, top-five status may be inevitable.

The Atlanta Hawks haven't shot the ball as well as they'd like this season. They're in the bottom third of the league in three-point percentage. And even a couple of the shooters who are supposed to buoy them in that category—Nickeil Alexander-Walker and CJ McCollum—are hovering around league average .

But the Hawks still have a top-10 net rating because of a long, swarming defense featuring Dyson Daniels (4.6 defensive rebounds and a league-leading 3.0 steals), Onyeka Okongwu (5.9 defensive rebounds, 0.9 steals and 0.8 blocks in 30.9 minutes) and Jalen Johnson (7.5 defensive rebounds and 1.1 steals).

When all three are on the floor, Atlanta allows just 105.7 points per 100 possessions (a defensive rating that ranks in the 92nd percentile).

The Detroit Pistons closed out their week with a blowout win over the Orlando Magic in a game Cade Cunningham didn't play. And of course, they've still only had Jalen Duren for two games all season.

So what is it that makes Detroit so competitive regardless of who's available (and actually better in terms of point differential when Cunningham is off the floor)?

There's clearly a culture with this team that transcends availability. No matter who's playing, the Pistons play hard. And there may not be anyone who exemplifies that better than Ausar Thompson.

After totaling 10 rebounds, seven assists and four blocks in Tuesday's win, Thompson is at 10.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 5.4 assists, 1.6 steals and 1.0 blocks in 29.4 minutes this season.

So why is his team sliding a bit in the rankings? All of the above didn't prevent them going 1-2 this week and holding off several teams that are surging.

And whenever Duren and Cunningham are back full time, the Pistons should recover a higher spot on this list pretty quickly.

Klay Thompson isn't the defender he once was. And he almost never gets to shots inside the three-point line (he's averaging a career-low 2.4 two-point attempts per game).

But his shooting is among the biggest reasons for the Miami Heat's early-season turnaround.

Over his last 11 games, Thompson is averaging 17.4 points and 4.5 threes, while shooting 45.0 percent from deep. And for the entire season, his plus-7.4 net rating swing is tied with Giannis Antetokounmpo for the best mark on the team.

9. Philadelphia 76ers (15-4): Tyrese Maxey

On a star-laden roster that includes four top-three picks in the starting lineup, it's the guard the Philadelphia 76ers took with the 21st pick in 2020 that has them in first place in the East.

No team in the league has played in more games that entered "clutch" time this season (when a game is within five points in the final five minutes), and Philadelphia is 12-0 in those games, thanks in large part to Maxey.

Beyond being the Sixers' top scorer at 25.9 points per game, Maxey also leads the team in total points scored in the clutch and is shooting 50.0 percent from the field in those minutes.

The concerning part, of course, is that Philadelphia needs clutch time in so many of these wins. Real title contenders typically blow more teams out, but the 76ers would obviously rather be winning than losing these contests.

The Memphis Grizzlies have had 18 different players suit up for them this season. Seventeen are at zero or better in the plus-minus column and four are already over 100 there.

It doesn't seem to matter who's on the floor for this team. It always plays hard. It always plays unselfish. And the ball screen-heavy system it plays empowers everyone.

That's why, despite absences from Ty Jerome, Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey, this team just keeps piling up wins and currently has the fourth best net rating in the NBA.

7. Portland Trail Blazers (12-6): Balance

We're now approaching December. The Portland Trail Blazers are tied for the fifth-best offensive rating in the league. And they've only had four individual performances of at least 30 points (all of which have come in the last two weeks).

Under first-year coach Micah Nori, the Blazers are moving the ball and spreading shots and playmaking opportunities all over the roster.

They have four players averaging at least four assists. They have eight players averaging at least eight points.

And that balance makes Portland one of the least predictable attacks in the game.

6. Boston Celtics (12-6): The Three-Point Line

They snapped it on Tuesday, but the Boston Celtics played through part of a four-game losing streak this week. And one of their biggest weaknesses was on display during the lull.

Without Jaylen Brown, Boston is light on rim pressure and as dependent on threes as they've maybe ever been (which is saying a lot, given Joe Mazzulla's years-old desire to see as many threes go up as possible).

On the nights when it's working (like it was Tuesday, when they hit 22 threes against the Washington Wizards), the Celtics look like a contender. They're now 5-1 when they connect on at least 20 triples.

And while that play style leads to a lot of variability, it also means they can beat anyone on any given night.

5. Los Angeles Lakers (15-3): Austin Reaves

Luka Dončić's slump is still on, as he shot 8-of-24 against the Utah Jazz to close out the week and is now at 40.1 percent from the field over his last six games.

It's not hard to put two and two together on this. The first game of this Luka run was also the one Austin Reaves left early. And he hasn't been on the floor since.

It's pretty clear now that his secondary ball-handling and the attention he commands from opposing defenses is going to be crucial for a real playoff run.

This season, when Reaves is on the floor, Luka is averaging 40.2 points per 75 possessions with a 69.2 true shooting percentage. When Reaves is off, those numbers for Luka drop to 33.0 and 55.6.

4. Houston Rockets (14-5): Extra Possessions

The Houston Rockets have the best offense and the third best effective field-goal percentage in the NBA.

And while hot shooting from Alperen Şengün, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith and Bogdan Bogdanović has a lot to do with that, one of Houston's strengths from last season may be driving their success on that end as much as anything.

The Rockets are second in the league in offensive rebounding percentage and third in second-chance points per game. And all the extra possessions created by Şengün, Steven Adams and Amen Thompson have opposing defenses flummoxed.

3. Minnesota Timberwolves (14-5): The Leap

The Minnesota Timberwolves could've nosedived off the contenders' tier when Anthony Edwards underwent a knee surgery that will cost him a significant chunk of this season, but they're first in the league in defensive rating, second in net rating and fourth in winning percentage.

And while there's plenty of credit to go around—LaMelo Ball's playmaking and Rudy Gobert's defense have been huge—the leap Jaden McDaniels has made has been more important than anything.

Without Edwards, McDaniels has taken on significantly more scoring and playmaking responsibilities, and he's putting up career highs in points (19.2), rebounds (6.4) and assists (3.8) while still dominating games as a perimeter defender.

2. New York Knicks (12-6): Karl-Anthony Towns

Jalen Brunson's true shooting percentage is well below average this season. Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges are both averaging under 10 points per game and shooting a combined 29.0 percent from three. All three of them have negative net rating swings.

But the New York Knicks are still 12-3 since their 0-3 start, and no one deserves more credit for that than Karl-Anthony Towns.

KAT is having the best season of his decorated career, posting a career-high 8.0 box plus/minus and averaging 21.2 points, a league-leading 13.6 rebounds and 4.2 assists, while shooting 41.7 percent from three.

When Towns is on the floor, the Knicks are plus-13.4 points per 100 possessions. When he's off, they're minus-4.0.

Victor Wembanyama, who's still just 22 years old, is already putting together an almost insurmountable "best in the world" case. Even in a season in which Luka Dončić is averaging 36.6 points, a Wemby MVP almost feels like a no-brainer.

The San Antonio Spurs' star leads the league in every major, publicly available catch-all metric. He's the best defensive player in the world. And his per-game averages of 30.7 points, 12.5 rebounds, 3.8 blocks, 3.2 assists and 1.3 steals, to state the obvious, have never been reached before. And he's putting them up in 30.5 minutes.

Did I mention he hasn't even turned 23 yet?

articles.title: NBA Cup 2026 Full Bracket Clinching and Elimination Scenarios for Nov. 27 Schedule
articles.summary: Eight teams advance through the Group Stage of the NBA Cup to make the Knockout Round.
articles.body:
Eight teams advance through the Group Stage of the NBA Cup to make the Knockout Round.

Only one spot has been secured so far—by the Dallas Mavericks, who had their Knockout ticket punched during the Houston Rockets' win over the Phoenix Suns on Wednesday.

Five of the remaining unsecured spots will go the other Group winners. The last two will land with the Wild Card winner from each conference—the team with the best record among non-Group winners or, if a tiebreaker is needed, the one with the best point differential during Group Play games.

With so much still at stake ahead of the Group Stage's final game night, let's set the stage for where things stand and look ahead at the clinching scenarios in play for Friday night.

Philadelphia (2-1; -12 point differential)

San Antonio (2-1; +48 point differential)

* x-clinched group; e-eliminated from knockout contention

Full Clinching Scenarios for Friday Night

The full list of clinching scenarios runs deep. Don't worry, though, as we'll provide a viewing guide for the must-watches on Friday.

If you're interested in seeing teams in total control of their fate, you're in luck. Three of Friday's contests have true win-and-you're-in stakes. Well, for one side of the matchup, at least.

It starts with the Philadelphia 76ers visit to the Indiana Pacers (7:30 p.m. ET). Since the Sixers already have the head-to-head edge on the Miami Heat, Philly will lock up East Group B with a win over Indiana regardless how Miami fares against the New York Knicks.

A little later, the Boston Celtics host the Atlanta Hawks (8 p.m. ET) with both teams in control of their Group C destiny. A Celtics' win would push their Group Play record to a perfect 4-0 and crown them as Group C champs. A Hawks' win, meanwhile, would put both teams at 3-1 and give Atlanta the Group C title for its head-to-head advantage.

In West Group B, it all comes down to the Memphis Grizzlies' road game with the Minnsota Timberwolves (8:30 p.m. ET). The Timberwolves would secure a 4-0 record and give them the group outright, while a Grizzlies' victory would mean both clubs finish 3-1 and Memphis gets the head-to-head nod.

Elsewhere, in the West Group C (Los Angeles Lakers at San Antonio Spurs; Golden State Warriors at Portland Trail Blazers) and East Group A (Milwaukee Bucks at Detroit Pistons; Brooklyn Nets at Toronto Raptors), multiple teams will carry 2-1 records into have-to-have-them games. A win alone won't decide the groups, which will rely on other results or point-differential tiebreakers to determine the group champ.

articles.title: How Savannah James makes her money: Inside her $100 million net worth, business contracts and growing investment empire
articles.summary: Savannah James now earns from a skincare line, a podcast, a paid membership community and an investor stake in a pro volleyball team.
articles.body: Savannah James now earns from a skincare line, a podcast, a paid membership community and an investor stake in a pro volleyball team. The entrepreneur, estimated at $100 million in net worth, folded the podcast and membership into a holding company called Signed in June 2026. MarcyPen Capital Partners, the firm Jay-Z co-founded, backed the launch. She is married to NBA star LeBron James, but her ventures stand apart from his earnings. The size of her stakes has not been made public, and neither have the valuations of the companies.How does Savannah James make her money?Savannah James earns through businesses she owns or co-owns, and most of them launched in the last two years. The $100 million entrepreneur started Reframe in May 2025, a skincare line with three products priced at $115, $95 and $135. The company says a year-long Howard University study with 50 participants of different ages and skin tones backs the formulas.James began the podcast Everybody's Crazy in April 2024 with her friend April McDaniel. It started on the Dear Media network, then went independent, which gave the pair control over production and advertising deals. Let It Break came in November 2024. Members pay $250 a month on an annual commitment.McDaniel, who founded the creative agency Crown + Conquer in 2016, is a full business partner. The two have spoken openly about living on different budgets. On Boardroom's Mental Wealth podcast, James said, "My friends are very respectful of my situation."What has Savannah invested in lately?The biggest move is Signed. James and McDaniel announced the holding company in June 2026, and it puts Crown + Conquer, Let It Break and the podcast under one roof. MarcyPen Capital Partners came in as the backer. Neither the amount nor James' ownership share has been disclosed. In a September 2026 Boardroom interview, she explained that she had self-funded her earlier ventures and saw outside money as a new responsibility.Sports came next. In September 2026, the volleyball investor joined the group behind the Los Angeles Orbit, a League One Volleyball team that plays at the Intuit Dome beginning with the 2026-27 season. Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian leads the group, and Issa Rae is also in. James wanted to back a pro team that gives young athletes role models. Her check size is not public either.Not every bet worked out. She opened the Juice Spot in Miami's Brickell area in December 2013 and closed it in January 2016, after the family moved back to Ohio and daily oversight got hard.The $100 million figure is an estimate with gaps. It blends her business interests with her place in a wealthy household, and none of the company valuations are public.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

The final day of NBA Cup group play is on Friday, with seven of the eight spots still up for grabs (only the Dallas Mavericks have clinched a spot) in the knockout stage, which will take place Dec. 4-11.

Who will advance? Here's a look at the current standings, remaining schedule and clinching scenarios for Friday.

TOR loss + ATL loss + MIA loss + DET wins tiebreaker in Group A and over any second-place team from Group B or C

Clinches Group C and home-court in knockout round with a win

Clinches Group B and home-court in knockout round with a win

DEN loss + MIN wins tiebreaker over second-place team in Group C

Win tiebreaker over DEN + second-place team in Group C

Eliminated with a loss + SAS win + POR win

Spurs, Lakers, Blazers, Warriors still alive

LA Lakers at San Antonio, 9:30 p.m. (Prime)

The eight teams that advance from group play will take part in a single-elimination tournament. The NBA Cup quarterfinals will be held on Dec. 4 and 5, with the semifinals on Dec. 8 and/or 9, with the higher-seeded teams hosting matchups in their home arenas. The top two teams will advance to the NBA Cup Final on Dec. 11.

Players of the teams that participate in the knockout stage will earn prize money.

(During the knockout stage, the 22 teams that didn't qualify will each play two to-be-determined, regular-season games.)

Where will the NBA Cup Final take place this year?

The NBA Cup is leaving Las Vegas, where the league has held the semifinals and championship game for the past three years. This year, the final will be held at Butler's Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis .

articles.title: Ricky Rubio da el salto a los despachos: entra en el accionariado del nuevo Joventut
articles.standfirst: Formará parte del accionariado del grupo empresarial lituano Confluence Valley, nuevo propietario del club badalonés
articles.summary: Formará parte del accionariado del grupo empresarial lituano Confluence Valley, nuevo propietario del club badalonés
articles.body: El base del Asisa Joventut Ricky Rubio formará parte del accionariado del grupo empresarial lituano Confluence Valley, nuevo propietario del club badalonés, según ha confirmado este viernes la entidad verdinegra. Los intereses de Ricky Rubio, una de las figuras más emblemáticas de la historia de la 'Penya', estarán representados por su agente, Edgar Pérez, que pasa a ser miembro del nuevo consejo de administración, en el que permanecerá el actual presidente, Juanan Morales. Los nuevos miembros del órgano directivo del club serán el consejero delegado de Confluence Valley y exCEO de la Euroliga, Paulius Motiejūnas, Eduard-Joseph Scott, director de operaciones de la Euroliga durante 15 años, y Emilis Vaitkaitis, director de operaciones del grupo lituano. La Junta de Accionistas del Joventut Badalona ha aprobado hoy, con el 99,9% de los votos el cambio de propiedad, anunciado el pasado 23 de octubre. Una operación que supone la venta de la entidad por parte de Scranton Enterprises a Confluence Valley. El nuevo propietario, que también lo es del Zalgiris Kaunas y del London Lions, ha expresado su compromiso de preservar la identidad del Joventut y de fortalecer su ambición de crecimiento como club deportivo. "Estamos satisfechos de haber completado esta transacción y de tener la oportunidad de contribuir al futuro de uno de los clubes de baloncesto más distinguidos de Europa", ha remarcado Paulius Motiejunas, consejero delegado de Confluence Valley. Motiejunas ha destacado "las tradiciones sólidas, una academia excepcional y un potencial de crecimiento significativo" como las fortalezas del Joventut. "Vemos oportunidades para fortalecer las operaciones comerciales del club y crear las condiciones para un crecimiento continuo los próximos años", ha añadido. El próximo miércoles 9 de diciembre, se celebrará una rueda de prensa en el Olímpico de Badalona para presentar la nueva estructura de propiedad y la visión de futuro del club por parte de la misma.
