articles.title: No. 1 seed MSU women's soccer cruises into Sweet 16 with rout of 8-seed Xavier
articles.summary: MSU jumped out to a 3-0 lead at halftime and rolled from there to advance to the Sweet 16 of the NCAA tournament for the fourth consecutive season.
articles.body:
The No. 1-seeded Michigan State women's soccer team set its sights on a familiar foe in the second round of the NCAA tournament in No. 8-seed Xavier.

The Spartans , who topped the Musketeers 2-0 to open the regular season, sprinted out to a commanding 3-0 lead at halftime in their rematch on Friday, Nov. 27, and cruised into the Sweet 16 for the fourth consecutive season with a 6-2 win at DeMartin Stadium.

MSU picked up right where it left off in its 7-0 win in the first round Nov. 21 over Central Connecticut State as senior forward Kayla Briggs found the back of the net before a minute had elapsed off the clock on Friday for her ninth goal of the season.

The First-Team All-Big Ten forward would then set up senior Emerson Sargeant for the Spartans ' second goal 10 minutes later.

Junior forward Shelby Vaughn added MSU's third goal late in the first half off an assist from Bella Najera, who continued to build off her two-goal performance in the opening-round win.

MSU continued to pile on at the start of the second half, with Sargeant feeding sophomore Ava Lutke for her first goal of the season. That setup gave Sargeant 25 assists for her career, tying former Spartan Laura Heyboer for the school record.

Senior forward Kennedy Bell would join the party in the 50th minute, scoring her 11th goal to give MSU a 5-0 lead.

Five minutes later, Briggs controlled a throw-in, navigated around Xavier's back line, and delivered a shot into the right corner of the net for her second of the game, putting MSU up 6-0 and giving MSU 13 goals in its two NCAA tournament games.

The Musketeers avoided the shutout with a header off a set piece in the 63rd minute to get on the board and prevent a second straight clean sheet for the Spartans. Xavier was then able to another goal late in the second half to account for the 6-2 final.

MSU will face now No. 4-seed Kansas at 6:30 p.m. Nov. 30 at DeMartin, looking to advance to the program's second consecutive Elite Eight.

articles.title: Sadler and Bizjack score 15 apiece, West Virginia beats UNC 72-59 at Dick Vitale Invitational
articles.summary: (AP) — Miles Sadler and Finley Bizjack each scored 15 points to help West Virginia beat North Carolina 72-59 on Friday night at the Dick Vitale Invitational....
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — Miles Sadler and Finley Bizjack each scored 15 points to help West Virginia beat North Carolina 72-59 on Friday night at the Dick Vitale Invitational.

Javan Buchanan had 11 points and eight rebounds for West Virginia (5-2) and Joson Sanon also scored 11.

The Mountaineers, who lead the series with North Carolina 6-0, never trailed. Bizjack and Sanon hit back-to-back 3-pointers to cap a 10-2 opening run and the Mountaineers scored nine consecutive points to push their lead to 16 points when Sanon made another 3 with 2:22 left until halftime.

West Virginia had eight steals in the first half as the scored 10 points off 10 UNC turnovers to take a 41-30 lead into halftime.

Maximo Adams led North Carolina (5-2) with 16 points. Jaydon Young scored 13 and Matt Able 12.

Somerville hit a 3 and followed with a jumper that gave the Mountaineers their biggest lead at 58-39 with 9:53 left in the game, but Able answered with a 3-pointer and Adams converted a three-point play before Able hit two more 3s in a 12-0 run that trimmed the deficit to seven points with 7:28 to go.

West Virginia got no closer as Sadler, Bizjack and Buchanan hit consecutive 3s that made it 67-41 and it was a double-digit lead the rest of the way.

articles.title: Kugel, Johnson and Bol propel UCF to 88-76 victory over Georgia at ESPN Events Invitational
articles.summary: (AP) — Riley Kugel and Dior Johnson both scored 24 points, and John Bol posted a double-double to lead UCF to an 88-76 victory over Georgia on Friday night i...
articles.body:
KISSIMMEE, Fla. (AP) — Riley Kugel and Dior Johnson both scored 24 points, and John Bol posted a double-double to lead UCF to an 88-76 victory over Georgia on Friday night in the Magic Bracket of the ESPN Events Invitational.

Johnson made 8 of 16 shots with two 3-pointers and all six of his free throws for the Knights (5-3), who bounced back from a 75-73 loss to Boston College in Thursday's opener. Kugel hit 7 of 13 shots with four 3-pointers and 6 of 7 at the foul line. Bol totaled 13 points and 14 rebounds.

Kanon Catchings finished with 21 points, eight rebounds, four assists and four steals to pace the Bulldogs (6-2), who led 24-12 midway through the first half. Blue Cain and Freddie Dilione V both scored 14 with Cain adding seven assists and six of Georgia's 13 turnovers.

Reserve Carmelo Pacheco scored all 12 of his points in the first half on 4-for-4 shooting from 3-point range and UCF took a 50-39 lead into the break. Kugel also had 12 points and Johnson added 11 for the Knights, who sank eight 3-pointers and shot 53% from inside and outside the arc.

UCF never trailed after Kugel followed his 3-pointer with a layup for a 38-37 lead with 3:17 left before halftime.

Georgia lost 83-81 to Cincinnati in its opener.
